subject: Interpreting the results from categorical predictors and the best was to predict using a large number of new points.

messages.author: 4c005f3884d0897f
messages.subject: Interpreting the results from categorical predictors and the best was to predict using a large number of new points.
parts:
I posted previously and I only recently started using Bayesian statistics so it's taking some time to get my head around it. I have two issues I need some help with: how to interpret the output of a model that includes a categorical predictor, and the best way to predict. I'm basically looking at the association between biomass and environmental variables. Soil types are the most important predictors. Part of my results are given below. Inla gives different parameters for each level of the predictor variable. How should this be interpreted? Does this mean only the levels with credible intervals that do not include zero are important, and these are the only ones that should be reported? So should the others be removed for predictions? Also, and this might sound like a silly question, but if all the levels of the categorical predictor has a credible interval that includes zero, does this mean that the categorical predictor isn't important? I found that this was the case for a categorical predictor, but it was the best predictor (with a correlation coefficient of 0.42 between the predicted and observed values, with no other predictor coming close).

Also, I'd like to predict biomass at new locations. A soil map was converted to a point shp. file and the coordinates and the soil types were appended to the attribute table of each point. This was saved as a csv file and imported into R. I tried to use these to create a joint stack to facilitate predictions at each point. I removed soil types that were not sampled in the data used to build the model. I have 9 million points/locations where I need to predict biomass, and due to computational issues, I decided to predict only for 200k points at a time. I tried the methods below, but depending on the number of points used, and the method I used, the correlation between the observed and the predicted values from the single stack model, was never the same as the joint model (it was often much lower than the single stack model). Moreover, the mean values for each level of the categorical variable were very different. If the number of points used is 1k or 10k everything is fine. If I use 100k points then the results become wacky. The only method that works but has a lower correlation coefficient (single stack 0.82 versus joint stack 0.77), is the method that doesn't include a spatial term (method 4 below). I would prefer to include a spatial term updated with the new points where the predictions will be made.  So I'm trying to determine if I am doing something wrong, and the best way to get consistent values. Finn suggested using Inla.posterior.sample, but I am not sure that this method takes into consideration the category level at the new points for which the prediction is sought. I also include a random error in the single stack model. whether this is included or not makes little difference... I still get the same results. Can anyone help??

 

#-- Construct the SPDE object --#

spde = inla.spde2.matern(mesh=mesh, alpha = 2)

field.indices = inla.spde.make.index("field", n.spde=mesh$n)

A.est = inla.spde.make.A(mesh, loc=est.coord.1)

 

######For single variable soil..the best model

stack.est = inla.stack(data = list(AGB=est.data),

A = list(A.est, 1),

effects = list(c(field.indices), data.frame (Intercept=1, soil=biomass4$DOMSOI_12,  Plot = inla.group(biomass4$Plot))), tag="est")

 

formula <- AGB ~ -1 + Intercept + soil + f(Plot, model = "iid")+ f(field, model=spde)


####Joint stack

Apred6 <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh = mesh, loc = cbind(iDat.1$X, iDat.1$Y))


stack.pred.response <-inla.stack(data=list(AGB=NA), A=list(Apred6,1), effects=list(c(field.indices,list(Intercept=1)),list(soil=iDat.1$DOMSOI_12)), tag = "pred")

join.stack <-inla.stack(stack.est,stack.pred.response)

 

####Method 1

#-- Call INLA and get results --#

mod =   inla(formula,

             data=inla.stack.data(join.stack, spde=spde),

             family="gaussian",

             control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(join.stack), compute=TRUE), quantiles=NULL,

control.results=list(return.marginals.random=FALSE,

return.marginals.predictor=FALSE), verbose=TRUE)

 

###### Method 2

#-- Call INLA and get results --#

starting.value =   inla(formula, data=inla.stack.data(join.stack, spde=spde), family="gaussian",

             control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(join.stack), compute=TRUE),control.inla = list(diagonal =  100,strategy = "gaussian", int.strategy = "eb"), quantiles=NULL, verbose=TRUE, num.threads=6)


#-- Call INLA and get results --#

mod =   inla(formula,

             data=inla.stack.data(join.stack, spde=spde), family="gaussian", control.mode = list(result = starting.value, restart = TRUE), control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(join.stack), compute=TRUE), control.results=list(return.marginals.random=FALSE, return.marginals.predictor=FALSE), verbose=TRUE)


#########Method 3

#-- Call INLA and get results --#

mod.mode =   inla(formula, data=inla.stack.data(stack.est, spde=spde),

             family="gaussian",  control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stack.est), compute=FALSE),

                                verbose=TRUE)

 

#-- Call INLA and get results --#

mod.2 =   inla(formula, data=inla.stack.data(join.stack, spde=spde),

             family="gaussian",  control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(join.stack), compute=TRUE),

                                control.mode=list(theta=mod.mode$mode$theta, restart=FALSE), verbose=TRUE)


##########Method 4 no spatial term in prediction stack

stack.pred.response <-inla.stack(data=list(AGB=NA), A=list(1), effects=list(data.frame(Intercept=1,soil=iDat.1$DOMSOI_12,  Plot = inla.group(iDat.1$Plot))), tag = "pred")


stack.est = inla.stack(data = list(AGB=est.data), A = list(A.est, 1), effects = list(c(field.indices), data.frame (Intercept=1, soil=biomass4$DOMSOI_12,  Plot = inla.group(biomass4$Plot))), tag="est")


###Join stack

formula <- AGB ~ -1 + Intercept + soil + f(Plot, model = "iid")+ f(field, model=spde)
